issues.title: Docstring cites a pin test that does not exist; the load-bearing ordering is entirely unpinned
issues.description:
The rewritten `_classify_environmental` docstring asserts that the collateral-before-SEMAPHORE_TIMEOUT ordering 'REMAINS LOAD-BEARING (task 3679 review)', explains that reading collateral as a slot timeout 'would convert a self-recovering host condition into a blocking escalation', and closes with 'Pinned by ``TestAnchoredSlotTimeoutWithCollateralIsEnvTransient``.' It further states that the replayed 5164/5071 fixtures 'now pass structurally and pin nothing about this tie — which is exactly why the dedicated co-occurrence test above exists alongside them.'

That dedicated test was never written. `grep -rn 'AnchoredSlotTimeout\|WithCollateralIsEnvTransient' orchestrator/` returns nothing repo-wide. The only classes present are TestIncidentalTokenFaultsDispatchByTool (line 1085) and TestReplayedMergeVerifyCollateralWinsOverSemaphore (line 1477) — and the docstring itself correctly concedes the latter now pins nothing about this tie, since its fixtures contain no anchored marker.

I confirmed the documented behaviour is correct as written (anchored slot line + any of the three collateral shapes classifies env_transient in either concatenation order), so this is not a behavioural defect — it is a missing guard on an invariant the code documents as safety-critical, plus a docstring that makes a false claim about the repo's contents.
issues.failure_scenario: Mutation test, run and then reverted: moving the `if _SLOT_TIMEOUT_SENTINEL_RE.search(output) or _SLOT_ACQUIRE_DEADLINE_RE.search(output)` branch from last position to immediately above the `_VERIFY_ENV_BROKEN_RE` check changes classification of 'lib_test_semaphore.sh: failed to acquire test slot within 1800s (LOCK=/tmp/x.lock, N=8)\n' + 'shell-init: error retrieving current directory: getcwd: cannot access parent directories\n' from env_transient to semaphore_timeout. That converts a recoverable RetryKind.ENV_SERIAL condition into RetryKind.NONE, which terminates in a blocking human escalation — precisely the outcome the docstring says the ordering exists to prevent. Full suite result after the mutation: 514 passed. No test reds. A future refactor that reorders these branches ships the regression silently.
issues.recommendation: Add the cited class (or rename the docstring reference to a test that actually exists). A minimal version: assert that each of the three grounded collateral shapes concatenated with an anchored slot-timeout line classifies ENV_TRANSIENT in BOTH concatenation orders. Note the collateral fixtures must match the real patterns — `error retrieving current directory:\s*getcwd:`, `(?:^|/)verify\.sh: No such file or directory`, `^=== INTERRUPTED \(worktree removed\) ===` — a bare 'getcwd: cannot access parent directories' line does not match any of them.

issues.title: Emitter allowlist misses tree-sitter-generate.sh, an in-verify-path lock-acquisition deadline emitter
issues.description:
The allowlist comment states 'Each name is grounded in a line reify emits TODAY' and instructs 'Add a fourth name ONLY when a real emitted sample is observed.' Two such samples exist in reify today, from a script that is part of the verify plan:

  - reify scripts/tree-sitter-generate.sh:80 — `echo "ERROR: could not acquire flock within ${MAX_WAIT_SECS}s" >&2`, emitted when `flock -x -w $MAX_WAIT_SECS 9` misses its deadline
  - reify scripts/tree-sitter-generate.sh:111 — `echo "ERROR: could not acquire generation lock after ${MAX_LOCK_WAIT_SECS}s" >&2`, the mkdir-based fallback lock's deadline

That script is added to the verify plan at reify scripts/verify.sh:2028 (`add "./scripts/tree-sitter-generate.sh"`), so its stderr reaches this classifier. Both are genuine slot/lock-acquisition deadline events — the exact class of host condition SEMAPHORE_TIMEOUT exists to label — and neither matches `_SLOT_ACQUIRE_DEADLINE_RE` (different verb: 'could not acquire' rather than '<script>.sh: failed to acquire', and no allowlisted basename prefix).

This is not a regression: the deleted co-occurrence also missed both, since neither line carries a `\btimed?\s*out\b` token. But it means the task's headline goal — positive detection of the real event — is only partially achieved, and the completeness claim in the comment is inaccurate as written.
issues.failure_scenario: Verified against the live module on this branch: classify_failure(ToolKind.OPAQUE, 1, 'ERROR: could not acquire flock within 300s\n', False) returns unknown_test_failure, and 'ERROR: could not acquire generation lock after 600s\n' likewise returns unknown_test_failure. A real tree-sitter grammar-generation lock contention on a busy host is therefore labelled a code fault and routed to the debugger, instead of being labelled the infra-transient host condition it is.
issues.recommendation: Either extend the alternation with a fourth grounded entry for tree-sitter-generate.sh (its verb differs, so the pattern needs a second branch, not just another basename), or — consistent with the comment's own stated preference — leave the code as is and correct the comment to record this as a known, deliberately-out-of-scope emitter rather than implying the three-name list is exhaustive. The comment's own escape-hatch guidance (prefer `@@REIFY_SLOT_TIMEOUT@@` to a fourth basename) applies cleanly here and could be filed as the reify-side follow-up.

verdict.summary: The core change is sound and unusually well-grounded. I independently verified every producer claim against /home/leo/src/reify and all of them hold verbatim at the cited line numbers: lib_test_semaphore.sh:173, lib_lane_x_flock.sh:138, cargo-test-occt-gated.sh:182 (including its unique `ERROR: ` prefix); the `within unlimiteds` wart is real at lib_test_semaphore.sh:170-173, justifying `\S+s\b` over `\d+s`; and the docstring's claim that `flock -w` is absent from the slot path is accurate (lib_slot_acquire.sh uses non-blocking `flock -xn` in a shuffle loop). Replacing the whole-output lock+timeout co-occurrence with a line-anchored positive detector is the right call and the incident analysis is correct. No orphaned references to the six deleted symbols remain; the `_PYTEST_FAILURE_SUMMARY_RE` in verify.py is the pre-existing, deliberately-duplicated one. The archive=True flip is consistent with FLOCK_ERROR's existing row and correctly derived through ARCHIVE_DENY_LIST. All 514 tests pass. Two issues found. The first is concrete and confirmed by mutation: the source docstring states the DISK_FULL/collateral/SEMAPHORE_TIMEOUT ordering "REMAINS LOAD-BEARING" and is "Pinned by TestAnchoredSlotTimeoutWithCollateralIsEnvTransient" — that class exists nowhere in the repo, and moving the slot arm above the collateral checks flips anchored-slot+collateral from env_transient to semaphore_timeout (self-recovering ENV_SERIAL retry to blocking RetryKind.NONE escalation) with all 514 tests still green. I did verify the ordering behaviour itself is exactly as documented; it is simply unpinned. The second is a grounding-sweep gap: tree-sitter-generate.sh is in reify's verify plan (verify.sh:2028) and emits two genuine lock-acquisition deadline lines that the allowlist misses, so they classify unknown_test_failure. Neither issue is a runtime regression, and both are contained fixes.
